title: Uncover a buried pipe with a spade without touching it
instruction: Dig the soil off the top of the yellow pipe between the white marks until the top of the pipe is bare along at least 8 cm. Never let the spade touch the pipe.
context: Before a trench is dug near a marked gas, water or power line, the crew uncovers the line by hand at the locate marks to confirm where it runs and how deep it is. The digging must stop short of the line: a spade that gouges a plastic gas pipe or nicks a cable causes a leak or a fault. The robot works a tool through loose fill toward an obstacle it can't see, taking shallower cuts as it gets close. Done by: construction laborers, utility locators and pipeline workers.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y left, z up from the worktop. Soil box: fixed grey open-topped channel 180 mm long (x 210-390) and 54 mm wide inside (y -237 to -183) on the worktop, 6 mm walls; side and far walls 60 mm high, near wall (nearest the arms) 24 mm high; white marks across the side-wall tops at x 250 and 350. Gas pipe: fixed yellow tube 25 mm across on the worktop along the channel's middle (axis y -210), x 210 to 420, its top at z 25. Soil: 156 brown 12 mm wooden cubes, 1.2 g, in 13 rows (x 216.5-368.9, 12.7 mm pitch): two outer columns 4 high beside the pipe, two inner columns 2 high on it, about 25 mm over the pipe; last 15 mm before the far wall empty. Spoil board: fixed, 100 x 120 x 4 mm at x 150, y -210. Spade: loose, 70 g, green 16 x 24 x 90 mm handle on a 3 mm steel blade 42 wide x 35 tall, standing in a fixed slotted holder at x 300, y -330.
scoring: Strike: any contact between the spade and the pipe scores 0 for the trial (real: chalk on the pipe, any mark on the spade; sim: any spade point within 1 mm of the pipe). The pipe's top is the 10 mm strip along its crown; the marked stretch is judged in twenty 5 mm segments, bare when no cube lies over the strip, seen from above. Best level reached with the cubes in the box still for 1 s: 1.0 at 80 mm or more bare (trial ends); 0.5 at 40 mm; 0.25 at 10 mm; otherwise 0. The grippers may touch the pipe, and where the soil goes doesn't matter.
reset_notes: Stand the spade back in its holder, rebuild the cube lattice, and wipe and re-chalk the pipe.
fidelity: Soil is 12 mm rigid cubes: they hold a cut face like damp soil but are far coarser. Pipe and box are fixed. A strike is judged geometrically (1 mm approach), not by force, so any touch counts. The YAM wrist is compliant: the blade rides up as it drags and the arm settles about 1.5 mm low with the spade held.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 in 2,400 actions (spade never picked up). Scripted YAM demo: 1.0 in about 1,170 actions (100 mm bare, closest approach 3.3 mm).
